model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary shareholders less CET1 retention, net debt zero, USD flows bridged to the HKD quote

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average (years 1-10); equity CAGR rejected (see warning) and the 5yr revenue/EPS CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID/zero-rate/2.3bn-impairment trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3-2.6%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (7.3-8.7%) and EPS (31-79%) CAGRs. Cause: $8.5bn of buybacks FY2019-FY2025 plus rising dividends keep ordinary equity flat (shares in issue 3,340M -> 2,247M) while per-share earnings compound, and FY2020 is a rate/credit trough that inflates every 5yr CAGR. Neither series is a forward growth rate; the base case uses management's 5-7% income target to 2028, fading to 3%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: bank OCF/FCF is meaningless (deposit and trading-balance flows). SBC is ~1.9% of revenue, rising from 1.1% in FY2020 as deferred bonus regulation changed; it does not distort growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Standard Chartered delivers most, not all, of its May-2026 plan. Income grows 6% in 2026 and ~5% a year to 2028 on Wealth Solutions, network/financial-institution income and digital-asset optionality; NII is flat-to-low-single-digit as global rates fall. Costs are held near $13.3bn and the final Fit for Growth charges roll off, taking the reported margin from 31.6% (FY2025) to 38% by 2029 and RoTE to ~16.5% against the >15% 2028 target. CET1 is held at 14% and ~60-80% of earnings go out as the 30%+ dividend plus rolling buybacks. After 2029 the loan-loss rate normalises toward 30bp and returns fade to ~15%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The plan lands in full and the ~18% RoTE 2030 ambition is met and sustained. Affluent net new money reaches $200bn by 2028, Wealth Solutions compounds at double digits, CIB network income reaches ~70% of CIB income, Mox and Trust reach profitability, and the digital-asset/tokenisation franchise becomes a visible fee line. Cost:income falls through 57% on the headcount programme, credit costs stay ~20bp, and the bank keeps buying back 4-5% of its shares a year.
scenario_narratives.bear: The super-connector model meets a closed corridor. US-China escalation and a Middle East shock cut trade and flow income in 2027 while rate cuts erode NII; a China/HK CRE and frontier sovereign cycle (Ghana/Nigeria/Pakistan-style devaluations) lifts credit impairment to the FY2020 level and a conduct/AML charge recurs. CEO succession lands badly after the 2026 CFO departure. Returns recover only to ~12% RoTE, roughly the pre-2023 franchise plus the cost savings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Standard Chartered is valued as the cash its ordinary shareholders can take out: profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (after AT1/preference coupons and NCI) less the CET1 retained to hold 14% of RWA as the balance sheet grows, discounted at an 11% USD cost of equity. Deposits and MREL are funding, not debt, so net debt is zero and nothing is deducted after the flows. USD per-share values are converted to the HKD quote at spot; the HKEX line is the same ordinary share as STAN.L.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: FY2025's 19bp loan-loss rate is a trough for an EM book (65bp in FY2020); every 10bp is ~$0.35bn pre-tax
Rate sensitivity: NII (54% of income) guided flat-to-low-single-digit as global policy rates fall; a faster cutting cycle moves the base toward the bear
US-China / Middle East geopolitics: the network-income model depends on open corridors and the bank carries conflict-risk overlays
Notable items: $937m in FY2025, $797m in FY2024; the base assumes they stop after the final FFG year in 2026
CET1 retention is tied to revenue 1:1 and held at 14.0%; at 13.5% with RWA growing slower than income, value is ~5-8% higher
Data gap: H1-2026 interim and Q3-2026 update not in core_metrics; share count is the 26-Jan-2026 post-buyback count, not today's (~4% lower, value-neutral by construction)
FX: HKD quote vs USD flows; the peg makes this a small risk but refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 143.0-248.8; parity cross-checked against STAN.L x GBPUSD
data_sources.financials: Standard Chartered Annual Reports FY2018-FY2025 (research/2888.HK/Extracted), 2888.HK_Metrics.csv and kpis (core_metrics); FY2025 capital section (:4075-4105), summary table (:1260-1300), per-share data (:3655-3672), diluted shares (:23422)
data_sources.qualitative: 2888.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-22), including H1-2026 (29-Jul-2026), Q3-2026 trading update (1-Oct-2026) and 19-May-2026 capital markets day headlines

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ordinary shares at the FY0 balance-sheet date (31-Dec-2025), consistent with FY0 = FY2025 and year 1 = FY2026: 2,247M ordinary shares in issue at period end (2888.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:3667) less 9.1M bought in Jan-2026 to complete the $1.3bn programme (62.2M total, 53.1M by 31-Dec; the full $1.3bn was already deducted from CET1 at 31-Dec-2025, :4090-4100) = 2,238M, plus 71M dilutive potential shares (FY2025 diluted weighted 2,404M vs basic 2,333M, :23422) = 2,309M. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are the distribution of the flow, value-neutral at IV. NOT reduced for the $1.5bn (Feb-2026) and $1.0bn (Aug-2026) 2026 programmes, which are funded from the FY2026 year-1 flow: using today's lower count (est. ~2,155M basic / ~2,225M diluted) together with the full year-1 flow would double-count. A 1-share-1-vote ordinary listing in Hong Kong (no ADS ratio): 2888.HK and STAN.L are the same share.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow 'Share-based payment costs (Note 31)' 399 (2888.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:22786; 334 in FY2024). Bank: last_fcf is FY2025 profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders 4,558 (profit for the year 5,097 less AT1/preference dividends 527 less NCI 12); reported_fcf = 4,558 + SBC 399. SBC nets out of the bank flow ('ebitda' adds it back, sbc_pct removes it); it only moves the street basis.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share buybacks 2,719 per the cash flow statement (capital table shows $2.8bn incl. the Jan-2026 completion). Ordinary dividends paid FY2025 954 (:21955); FY2025 declared dividend 61c/share (+65%). Since the balance-sheet date: $1.3bn programme completed 26-Jan-2026; $1.5bn programme announced 24-Feb-2026 (-58bp CET1 in Q1-26); $1.0bn programme announced 29-Jul-2026 with the H1-26 results (interim dividend 20.4c, +66%). Payout policy: dividends at least 30% of earnings, supplemented by buybacks.
inputs.fx_note: Flows, balance sheet and per-share values in the model are USD (Standard Chartered reports in USD although UK-domiciled). The quote is HKD per ordinary share on the HKEX secondary line. Model-to-quote rate 7.843 HKD per USD (Yahoo HKD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-22T06:39Z; the HKD is pegged at 7.75-7.85). Parity check against the primary London line: STAN.L 2,064p close 2026-10-21T17:59Z x 1.3405 GBPUSD = US$27.67 per share; the 2888.HK quote at inputs.price_as_of divided by 7.843 lands within 2% of that (different sessions: London 21-Oct close vs HK 22-Oct intraday), confirming the rate, its direction and that no share-ratio applies. USD flows are discounted at a USD cost of equity and converted at spot. refresh_price.py moves the HKD price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T06:47Z HKEX regular session, live (Yahoo Finance chart API; 5d bars confirm trading through 22-Oct)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 11.0% in USD, the currency of the flows: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x 5.25% ERP = ~10.5%, plus ~0.5pp for frontier/EM sovereign and FX exposure (Ghana, Nigeria, Zambia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Egypt hyperinflation/devaluation episodes) and the AML/sanctions conduct history. Above HSBC (10.5%, Hong Kong concentration) and in line with BCS (11.0%); SC has no developed-market home franchise and its earnings are spread over ~54 EM/frontier markets. One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: the bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including occupancy and IFRS-16 depreciation/interest; no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - (AT1/preference dividends + NCI)/(1 - t), so the flow is profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders. FY2025: AT1 + preference 527, NCI 12 (KPI AT1PreferenceDividends; ProfitAttributableToOrdinary 4,558). AT1 par ($7.5bn other equity instruments) is therefore NOT also deducted in a bridge (HSBC/LYG/BCS convention). NCI is negligible (<0.3% of profit).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, net_debt = 0, the house precedent for large banks (HSBC, LYG, BCS, WFC, USB, NAB.AX). SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; FCFE-at-CoE with a CET1-retention charge is the same economics (value = TNAV + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and keeps 2888.HK comparable to HSBC/LYG. Deposits ($530bn customer accounts), debt securities in issue ($73bn) and subordinated liabilities ($8.8bn) are operating/MREL funding, not enterprise debt; OCF is meaningless (CSV swings -20.5bn to +36.8bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = reported operating income (CSV revenue) FY2025 20,942. 'ebitda' FY0 = PBT 6,963 + SBC 399 - (527 + 12)/(1 - 26.8%) 736 = 6,626 (31.64%). FY0 check: (6,626 - 399) x (1 - 26.8%) = 4,558 = reported profit attributable to ordinary. FY2025 reported PBT carries $937m of notable items (restructuring 320, Fit for Growth 531, DVA 31, other 55; underlying PBT 7,900), so year 1 steps up as FFG charges end in 2026 (the final year) and reporting moves to a reported basis. D&A = 0 (inside opex). 'capex' = CET1 retention holding CET1 at 14.0% of RWA (top of the 13-14% target range, where management actually runs: 14.1% Dec-25, 14.2% Jun-26 after buybacks) as revenue grows: 172.5 x g/(1+g), floored at zero. This is conservative on two counts: it ties RWA to revenue 1:1 (RWA grew 4.4% in 2025 vs income +7%, and op-risk RWA inflation is the main driver) and it holds 14.0% rather than the 13.5% midpoint (~$1.3bn, ~US$0.55/share, ~HK$4.3/share of surplus not credited). No equity_bridge item for surplus capital: the 0.1pp above 14.0% at Dec-25 was paid out through the Feb-2026 $1.5bn buyback, which is part of the year-1 distribution. TIMING: FY0 is FY2025 (31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, the latest filing in Extracted) and year 1 is FY2026E, discounted a full year although the valuation date is 10 months into FY2026; the ~8% of time-value forgone is roughly offset by the ~US$1.8/share of 2026 distributions (final 2025 dividend 49c, interim 20.4c, $2.5bn of buybacks) already paid to holders before today and still inside the year-1 flow. DATA GAP: the H1-2026 interim (29-Jul-2026) and Q3-2026 trading update (1-Oct-2026) are NOT in research/2888.HK/Extracted or core_metrics; their headline figures (H1 PBT $4.8bn record +9%, RoTE 17.6%, EPS 151.6c +17%, CET1 14.2%, FY26 income guidance raised to the middle of 5-7% cc, FY26 costs ex notables ~$13.3bn, NII low-single-digit growth) are taken from 2888.HK_Analysis.json and used only to set the year-1 path; the financial-parser should extract the interim so the next update can move FY0 to TTM Jun-26 and refresh the share count from a Total Voting Rights announcement.

bear.margin_rationale: An EM credit and FX cycle: faster global rate cuts compress NII, a US-China/tariff shock and Middle East escalation hit trade and Global Markets flow income (revenue -3% in year 2), China/HK CRE and frontier sovereign stress take credit impairment to ~$2.3bn (the FY2020 level, ~65bp of loans) in year 2, plus a legacy-style conduct charge. Margin troughs at 22% (PBT ~$5bn, still above any year before 2023) and recovers only to 30.5%: terminal RoTE ~12%, a thin spread over CoE. Retention floored at zero in the year-2 contraction (no capital release in a credit cycle).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (FY2026) 6.0%: guidance raised at H1-26 to the middle of the 5-7% constant-currency range and maintained at the Q3-26 update, with flow income growing >10% and NII low-single-digit; a weaker USD adds to reported growth. 2027-28 at 5.5%/5.0%, the lower half of the 5-7% 2025-28 target, then fading to 3% USD nominal by year 8.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 35.0% gives attributable profit ~$5.4bn (EPS ~244c vs 195.4c reported / 229.7c underlying in 2025) and RoTE ~13.5% on ~$40bn TNAV, consistent with H1-26 (RoTE 17.6%, EPS 151.6c) plus SC's seasonally weaker H2 and the final-year FFG charges. Margin rises to 38% by 2029 as cost:income heads toward the ~57% 2028 target and notable items stop (RoTE ~16.5%, just above the >15% 2028 target), then fades to 36.5% as the loan-loss rate normalises from 19bp toward ~30bp through the cycle and the rate tailwind is competed away. Terminal RoTE ~15%, a 4pt spread over the 11% CoE; management's ~18% 2030 ambition is NOT in the base.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention 172.5 x g/(1+g) holds CET1 at 14.0% of RWA as revenue grows. Implied distribution ~60% of attributable profit in year 1 (vs ~75% actual 2026 pace, because RWA grows slower than income) rising to ~80% at terminal.
base.tax_rationale: Reported ETR 26.8% in FY2025 (32.8% in FY2024; underlying 25.3%); 26% reflects the geographic mix shift that lowered 2025, UK bank surcharge on the (small) UK profit, Pillar Two top-ups and unrecognised UK deferred tax.

bull.margin_rationale: Management's May-2026 plan is delivered in full: income at the top of 5-7% through 2028 on Wealth Solutions double-digit growth ($200bn affluent NNM by 2028) and network income, cost:income to ~57% by 2028 and lower thereafter (>15% corporate headcount cut by 2030), credit costs stay ~20bp, and RoTE reaches ~18% by 2030 and holds. Terminal RoTE ~17.5-18%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): earnings are spread across ~54 EM/frontier markets with no developed-market home franchise, the business model is explicitly exposed to US-China and Middle East corridors, the AML/sanctions history is material, and CEO/CFO succession is unresolved. Base 50%: guidance has been raised once and maintained since; H1-26 was a record. Bull 25% (down from 35%): the bull requires the ~18% RoTE 2030 ambition to be met and held, and the shares at ~1.55x TNAV already price much of the plan.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.sanity_check_note: Known sanity_check.py fx-direction bug (see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug): historical_table() multiplies the HKD quote by fx_rate instead of dividing, inflating printed P/B (25.9x-80.2x) and P/Sales (73x-179x) by roughly fx_rate (7.843). Hand-bridged (price_usd = price_hkd / fx_rate): real FY2025 P/B 1.40x, P/S 3.12x -- unremarkable for a global bank. At the base-case IV (US$25.19): implied P/B 1.30x, P/S 2.89x, both inside the real historical range. Genuine pass; passed left true.
